 :Judgment:
This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Sri Sayi Kumar in the Road Traffic Accident dated 10.12.2022.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 10.12.2022 at about 10.00 a.m., when the petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KD- SCCH 15 3 MVC No.3517/2023 1640 along with his friend and when they reached in front of Aramane hotel, NH-206 road, Tarikere town, Chikkamagaluru, at that time,
respondent's Maruthi Alto Car bearing Reg.No.KA-18-P-4697 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) was driven in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and overtook another vehicle which was proceeding in front of it and all of a sudden came towards and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
As a result, petitioner and his friend fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries due to the impact of the accident.

3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, Tarikere, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Aradana hospital, Shivamoga and later shifted to RL Jalappa hospital, Kolar, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.2 remained absent and he was placed exparte.

The Respondent No.1 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.1 admitted that it has issued policy to the offending vehicle in favour of the respondent No.2.

Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.1 Sayi Kumar B.S vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120691876/
2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

sentences.text: The Respondent No.1 in its Objection Statement denied that the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 12.03.2025 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
 SCCH 15 5 MVC No.3517/2023  ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 10.12.2022 at about 10.00 a.m., in front of Aramane Hotel, NH-206 road, Tarikere Town, Chikkamagaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Maruthi Alto Car bearing Reg.No.KA-18-P-4697?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3) What Order or Award?
6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 20 documents.
7. Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.3517/2023  Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
REASONS 8. Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Maruthi Alto Car bearing Sayi Kumar B.S vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120691876/
3 Reg.No.KA-18-P-4697/offending vehicle.
9.

In this regard the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 09.12.2022 the petitioner and his friend Govardhan proceeded from Chikkaballapura to Muradeshwara and returning from Murudeshwara on 10.12.2022 and visited Jog and while returning at about 10.00 a.m., and when reached in front of Aramane hotel, NH-206 road, Tarikere town, Chikkamagaluru, at that time, the driver of the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and overtook another SCCH 15 7 MVC No.3517/2023 vehicle which was proceeding ahead of it and all of a sudden came and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the said impact, petitioner and his friend fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
10. The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 documents.
Ex.P1 is the FIR registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint given by Govardhan on 12.12.2022 as per Ex.P2.

As far as delay in lodging the complaint it is stated that since both the injured were under treatment in the hospital,
hence there is a delay in lodging the complaint.
Further Ex.P3 is the statement given by the petitioner before the police regarding the manner of the accident.

Ex.P4 is the spot mahazar which gives that details of the spot of the accident and spot of the accident is in front of Aramane hotel which is NH-206 Shivamogga - Tarikere road SCCH 15 8 MVC No.3517/2023 and width of the road is about 20 feet tar road and accident has occurred towards the edge of the road at distance of almost 5 feet.

Ex.P5 is the IMV report which indicates the damages sustained to the vehicles and the front side of the offending vehicle has been damaged which goes to show that the offending vehicle has dashed from front side to the bike of the petitioner resulting in the accident.
Ex.P6 is the wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the impact of the said accident.

Ex.P7 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC which discloses that the driver of the offending vehicle tried to overtake another vehicle and came to left side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner resulting in the accident.

Hence, on the basis of these documents produced by the petitioner it is satisfactorily established that the accident has occurred place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-
examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and in the cross-examination of PW.1 he has deposed that he was riding the motorcycle.
PW.1 admitted in his cross-examination he did not have DL, but had LLR and admitted that LLR is given to learn driving and he proceeded to go on tour on LLR with his friend in the bike.
It is admitted that it is the case of head on collusion.
He has deposed that Govardhan sustained minor injuries and denied that accident occurred due to his rash and negligent riding.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the petitioner's side nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner.

The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed Sayi Kumar B.S vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120691876/
4 about the manner of the accident.

sentences.text: The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross- examination of Respondent No.1.
There is no material on SCCH 15 10 MVC No.3517/2023 record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also denied the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.

The fact that the rider of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offences under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

Even though the rider was holding LLR there is nothing to indicate that the accident occurred due to the negligent riding of the motorist and it is the offending vehicle which went to overtake and to dashed the motor cycle.
In addition the motorist has gone a long distance driving and accident occurred when they were returning from tour which goes to show that he knew to ride motor cycle.

Hence in view of the SCCH 15 11 MVC No.3517/2023 said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver, driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

As far as the medical bills are concerned the petitioner has produced Ex.P8 - discharge summary of Jalappa hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 25.10.2023, underwent surgery on 30.10.2023 and discharged on 02.11.2023.
Ex.P6 is the wound certificate of Government hospital, Tarikere which discloses that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries due to the impact of the accident.
Ex.P9 are the photos that shows injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Ex.P12 SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3517/2023 & 15 are the medical bills.
Except suggesting that the bills are created nothing is elicited to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.
Hence petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.1,73,251/- under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P6 discloses that the petitioner has sustained deformity below the right knee, type III open fracture right tibia shaft middle to distal third, deformity above right ankle and multiple CLW over right lower leg and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and petitioner cannot do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.30,000/- is SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3517/2023 awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:

The petitioner was a student and was not earning and hence the loss of income during laid up period does not arise for consideration and hence the petitioner is not Sayi Kumar B.S vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120691876/
5 awarded any amount under this head.

sentences.text: 16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:
In his evidence PW.1 has submitted he was aged about 19 years and he was a student.

However for the purpose of assessing compensation it would be proper to assume the income as per the minimum wages chart wherein the income for the relevant period is ranging between 14,000 to 16,000/-
and hence the notional income is taken as Rs.15,500/- p.m for the purpose of assessing the loss of future income to the petitioner.

The petitioner has claimed in his affidavit he has permanent disability and as per the evidence of PW.2 his impairment is not progressive and will not improve in future and hence it is submitted by the petitioner that he cannot pursue his work as before the accident.

18. In support of the same, PW.2 - Orthopaedic Surgeon is examined and he has deposed that the petitioner has sustained deformity below the right knee, type III open fracture right tibia shaft middle to distal third, deformity above right ankle and multiple CLW over right lower leg.

PW.2 has deposed that petitioner is having difficulty to stand, unable to walk for long distance and climbing stairs, difficulty in standing on affected leg, not squatting, sitting cross legged, kneeling, taking turns and walk fast and run and assessed disability to the whole body at 16.8%.
He has deposed that fracture is united.
PW.2 is cross

- examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and in his cross-examination he has deposed he has not treated the petitioner and has SCCH 15 15 MVC No.3517/2023 assessed disability as per the 2018 guidelines and stated that there is no fracture in the joints and the implants are removed.
However taking into consideration the evidence of PW2 and other medical records it is just and proper to take 1/3rd of the said disability to the whole body.

Hence, the said disability assessed could be taken as 1/3 to the whole body, 1/3 of 16.8% is 5.6%
which is taken as disability to assess the compensation payable to the petitioner.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.15,500/- at the relevant time.
As far as, age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is concerned on perusal of the petitioner's Aadhaar card Ex.P11 the date of birth of the petitioner is 01.06.2004.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 10.12.2022 was around 18 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the SCCH 15 16 MVC No.3517/2023 judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '18' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of his above disability.

sentences.text: Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
18. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have taken the help of an attendant.
Further, he would be requiring conveyance for movement.
His avocation has been hit due to his disablement.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his SCCH 15 17 MVC No.3517/2023 treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.

20. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid NA up period 4.

Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  20,000/-
and conveyance 5. Medical expenses  1,73,251/-
6. Loss of Future Income 1,87,488/-
Total 4,30,739/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 4,30,739/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

sentences.text: Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.2 and has to pay compensation SCCH 15 19 MVC No.3517/2023 amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 and 2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 4,30,739/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E-payment and after proper identification.

The remaining 25%
award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
